steps.note: Group used to live only in the Layer menu and on Command G. This walk picks two layer rows, right clicks one of them and makes a group out of both from the row menu, then takes it apart again from the same menu. It also right clicks a row that is NOT in the selection, where Group has nothing to make a group out of and so is not offered.
two rows picked, the way a person picks the things they want held together
the menu on a picked row carries Group and Ungroup beside the arrange commands, with Command G printed against Group
the same menu on the row that was NOT picked: it is about that one row, and one row on its own has nothing to group, so no Group row
both picked rows went into one group; the row that was not picked stayed where it was
Ungroup out of the same menu put the two rectangles back loose

Merge Down out of the row menu used to take only the row it came from. On a picked row it now merges the whole selection into one, the same thing Command E does, so two of the three rectangles became one picture layer and the third is untouched.
